title: add ci artifact signing, provenance, and release manifests for private-installer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Add CI steps to produce signed release artifacts, SBOMs, and provenance/release manifests consumed by the private-installer and downstream customer validation. This enables reproducible, verifiable releases for VPC/on-prem installs and satisfies audit requirements from enterprise customers.

What this PR does: - Adds GitHub Actions workflow (ci/release-artifacts.yml) to: build release packages (helm charts, installer binaries, terraform modules), generate SBOMs with Syft, create in-toto provenance statements, and sign artifacts with cosign. - Produces a release-manifests/ directory containing a JSON manifest and per-artifact provenance files (in-toto link statements). - Uploads signed artifacts and manifests to the private-release S3 bucket and attaches them to the GitHub release. - Adds verification helpers used by the private-installer: a verify-release.sh script that checks cosign signatures and validates SBOM hashes before automated install/upgrade. - Updates Helm packaging pipeline to output chart tarballs with corresponding provenance and signature files. - Small docs update (docs/release/private-installer.md) describing verification steps for customers and internal runbook for operators.

Checklist: - [x] Build steps added for binaries, helm charts, terraform modules - [x] SBOM generation (Syft) and attachment - [x] Cosign signing + public key upload to release - [x] in-toto provenance manifest generation - [x] Upload artifacts + manifests to S3 and GitHub release - [x] Installer verification script and unit tests - [x] Integration run against staging release runner

Testing: CI runs include unit tests for verify script, integration test that downloads artifacts from staging S3 and verifies signatures and SBOMs, and an end-to-end deploy smoke test of private-installer in a local VM. Performance impact: none at runtime; adds a small cost to release pipeline for SBOM and signing steps.

Rollout and migration: New releases will include the manifests by default. Installer verifies when RELEASE_VERIFY=true (default for enterprise builds). Backwards compatibility: older releases without provenance are still supported; verification step is opt-in until all customers have migrated.

References: Linear ENG-1923, SEC-814, previous PRs around release manifests and signing (see pr-5710, pr-5601 for related CI pieces).

release_notes: Add CI pipeline to produce signed release artifacts, SBOMs, and in-toto provenance manifests for the private-installer. Includes verification helpers used by the installer to validate signatures and SBOMs. Improves supply-chain security and auditability for private/on-prem releases.
notes_for_ops: Operators: public cosign key is published to the GitHub release and S3 path. Use scripts/verify-release.sh to validate downloaded artifacts. See docs/release/private-installer.md for rotation/runbook.
risk_mitigation: Verification is opt-in via RELEASE_VERIFY flag for backward compatibility. Uploads use retries and are validated by integration tests; rollback is supported by pointing installer to previous release manifest.
